html:
Dvaravati was a Buddhist culture of the Mon people in central Thailand from about the 6th to the 11th centuries, with centres at Nakhon Pathom, U Thong and Lopburi.

Its towns were ringed by moats, and its artists carved Buddha images and wheels of the law in stone. Coins from Nakhon Pathom bear the name Dvaravati. It was in touch with India, the Pyu of Burma and the kingdoms of Cambodia.

From the 11th century it came under the Khmer Empire. Its Buddhism passed to the Thai states that rose later, such as Sukhothai. The Phra Pathom Chedi at Nakhon Pathom stands on a Dvaravati site. See Theravada.
sum: Dvaravati was a Buddhist culture of the Mon people in central Thailand from about the 6th to the 11th centuries, with centres at Nakhon Pathom, U Thong and Lopburi.
